chunks.title: About the Journal of the AI Universe
chunks.text: The Journal of the AI Universe (RKVarma AI Universe) publishes Daily AI News Updates only: the latest AI news across every dimension of human civilisation. It covers 50 non-overlapping AI projects, numbered 01–50, in seven groups. From 25 October 2026 each daily issue is an automatic headline digest: the headline, link, source name, date and the source’s reliability label, with no summaries and no posters. Empty projects are left out of the day’s issue. A simple headline-list PDF is offered for download. Curated by Dr.P.R.K.Varma, a cardiologist (M.D., D.M.). Contact: varma@aiuniversejournal.org. These are news headlines only, not medical, financial, legal or investment advice.

chunks.title: The editor, Dr.P.R.K.Varma
chunks.text: The editor is Dr.P.R.K.Varma, M.D., D.M., a cardiologist. ORCID iD https://orcid.org/0009-0002-4674-4403. The journal is an independent editorial project. Contact: varma@aiuniversejournal.org.

chunks.title: Editorial policies
chunks.text: Editorial policies cover sourcing, corrections, independence, use of AI tools, privacy and the licence. Only verified sources are used; every item links to its original source; each item belongs to exactly one of the 50 projects. Original journal content is licensed under CC BY-NC 4.0, credit Dr.P.R.K.Varma, Journal of the AI Universe. Linked sources belong to their owners. The site does not ask for, collect or store personal information from visitors and sets no cookies. Theme choice is saved only in the reader’s browser.

chunks.title: Privacy policy
chunks.text: The journal does not collect or store readers’ personal details or their Ask the Journal questions. Questions typed into Ask the Journal are sent to Google’s Gemini API so an answer can be written from the journal’s own pages, and are also sent through a Cloudflare Worker. On Google’s free Gemini tier, Google may use submitted content to improve its products (see Google’s Gemini API terms). The Worker does not log or store questions. Hosting (GitHub Pages) and Google Fonts receive ordinary technical request data. Full policy: the Privacy section of Editorial policies.

chunks.title: Licence and reuse
chunks.text: Unless otherwise stated, original content of the Journal of the AI Universe is licensed under CC BY-NC 4.0. Share and adapt for non-commercial purposes with credit to Dr.P.R.K.Varma, Journal of the AI Universe. Commercial use needs permission. Dr.P.R.K.Varma has placed his AI for Beginners slide decks (PowerPoint and PDF) and those YouTube videos in the public domain (CC0 1.0). That notice does not apply to the rest of the journal, headlines, linked sources, third-party content or unpublished books.

chunks.title: Search the journal
chunks.text: The journal has a search page that runs in the reader’s browser. Use it to find headlines, categories and pages. There is also a tags page, a weekly ‘Best of the week’ page, an AI trends page, an AI glossary and a Saved for later page.

chunks.title: Watch
chunks.text: The Watch page lists the journal’s videos: daily issue reels (the latest 14) and pinned series. AI for Beginners is a YouTube series by Dr.P.R.K.Varma, free to use (CC0 1.0). Sanskrit and AI is another pinned series. PPT slides on AI (the AI for Beginners slide decks) appear on Watch from 22 November 2026, with on-page viewers and PowerPoint and PDF downloads.

chunks.title: Books shelf
chunks.text: The Books page is a shelf of free, officially available books and tools useful for learning AI, curated by Dr.P.R.K.Varma. The journal does not host book PDFs and does not copy book text. Each entry links to the official record or site. The shelf has been on the journal since 17 November 2026.

chunks.title: Events ahead
chunks.text: The Events ahead page lists upcoming conferences, workshops, seminars and other AI events, taken from official event pages, organised by the 50 projects.

chunks.title: Research Papers Today
chunks.text: Research Papers Today lists peer-reviewed papers and preprints gathered for the journal, with links to the publisher, DOI or arXiv page.

chunks.title: Global AI Hardware & Software R&D Intelligence
chunks.text: The R&D Intelligence section tracks hardware and software research and development at major AI companies. A separate R&D feed is available.

chunks.title: Issue archive
chunks.text: The archive lists every daily issue of the journal, with links to the issue page and, where offered, the PDF.

chunks.title: Subscribe
chunks.text: Readers can subscribe to the journal’s RSS feed. An email newsletter is planned but is not open yet.

chunks.title: Latest issue (22 November 2026)
chunks.text: The latest daily issue is dated 22 November 2026. Open the issue page for that day’s headlines across the 50 AI projects. A swipe-mode card reader is available on issues from 16 November 2026.

chunks.title: How the daily issue is made
chunks.text: Each daily issue is built automatically from allow-listed news, research and events feeds. Items need an AI term in the headline, a reliability label, and a link to the publisher’s own page. There are no AI-written summaries in the digest. Categories are assigned by fixed rules. The 50 projects include, among others, 01 Filmmaking, 04 Healthcare, 05 Finance, 06 Law & Investigation, 37 Foundation Models & Assistants, 43 Governance, 47 Funding, 48 AGI & ASI, and 49 AI, Consciousness & Sanskrit LLM. Healthcare, psychology and related items are news headlines only, not medical advice.

chunks.title: Ask the Journal
chunks.text: Ask the Journal is a small chatbot on the site that answers questions only from the journal’s own pages: issues, categories, Watch, Books, About and policies. It is not the editor, and it is not a medical, legal or financial adviser. If it cannot find the answer in the journal, it says it does not know and suggests using search or the categories.

chunks.title: The 50 AI projects
chunks.text: The journal is organised into 50 non-overlapping AI projects in seven groups: Industries & Sectors (01–14), People & Life Stages (15–20), Culture & Belief (21–29), Science (30–35), AI Tech Stack (36–41), Society & Governance (42–47), and Future & Frontier (48–50). Each project has its own page with recent headlines.

Headlines: - Indian chip startup Bharat Semi lands $24M seed round as it eyes global AI sensor market (TechCrunch). - NVIDIA CEO Exit Risks AI Startup Funding (The Chosun Ilbo). - Fewer than 10 people, under a year old: Anthropic reportedly paid $400 million for this biotech AI startup ((The Economic Times)). - Starling founder Anne Boden plots new AI-powered bank (Sifted). - Etzioni on AI: Startup speed is not a strategy (GeekWire). - AI makes 2 Indian-origin founders world’s youngest self-made billionaires worth ₹40,000 crore each, beats Zuckerberg (Livemint). - AI Startup Offers $30,000 Signing Bonuses to Hire AI-Savvy Engineers (Seoul Economic Daily). - Exclusive | AI Startup LangChain More Than Doubles Its Valuation to $3 Billion (WSJ). - Sebi to issue AI usage guidelines for capital markets, focus on investor protection (YourStory (India)). - Measure AI by results, not number of agents deployed: Oracle senior executive (YourStory (India)). - Otter.ai’s CEO grew up with rationed food in China—now his AI startup makes $100 million a year (Fortune). - Space, sustainability, AI: test your business creativity with Edition 258 of our weekly quiz! (YourStory (India)). Research papers: - Memory × Self-Evolution: When Agents with Cognitive Frameworks Meet Market Paradigm Shifts in Investment (ACM International Conference on AI in Finance (ICAIF)).

chunks.title: 16 November 2026 — 49 AI, Consciousness & Sanskrit LLM
chunks.text: Issue of 16 November 2026, project 49 AI, Consciousness & Sanskrit LLM. Headlines: - AI and the consciousness illusion ((The Hindu)). - Visva-Bharati begins digitising rare manuscripts at the Lipika Manuscriptorium under Gyan Bharatam (UNI). - IIAS Shimla holds a national seminar on Indian Knowledge Systems and AI (Careers360 (PTI)). - AI in India's Gyan Bharatam drive to digitise Sanskrit and other manuscripts, including 42,000 at Kashmir University (The Week). Research papers: - Evaluating AI-Based Scaffolding for Learning Research Philosophies and Paradigms (International Conference on Education Research). - Pingala: Prosody-Aware Decoding for Sanskrit Poetry Generation (Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics IJCNLP-AACL 2026). - Swanada: Split-Encoder Capability-Routed Conformer CTC and Sub-30 MB On-Device Speech Recognition Across Twelve Scripts (arXiv (cs.SD)). - Pāṇinīya-Praveśa (Entering Pāṇini): The Aṣṭādhyāyī in 30 Days — Complete Editions in English and Hindi (Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)).
